Macro overlay — from their posts, not our data
An FOMC-week tape with two minds. iain, posting just before this run, is the skeptic: a low-volume push into declining moving averages, with half of FinTwit already wearing ATH hats — and his relative-strength reminder (don't trade RS while the market falls, track it) frames the whole window. Prof and DiCarlo are the semiconductor bulls: Prof calls another failed breakdown in SMH plus bullish seasonality (“Lord Help Bears”), DiCarlo says the SMH bull cycle is still hanging on with structure bullish — but both put their exact levels in videos, not in visible posts. Remz is the tape-reader: the Nasdaq has gone nowhere in six months ($722.03 on May 14, $721.25 today), and the move out of it “is going to blow your mind.” Enrich ran the busiest board again: a 10/28 watchlist (RKLB, TSLA visible), Leadr's daily top 5 (NOW, AAPL, PLTR, KO, SPCX), a rotation note into software ahead of FOMC, and the “It's All Over” portfolio whose list cuts off after CIFR. Venu supplied the fundamentals: FSLY's multi-year base with accumulation, AVGO's Anthropic angle, and the warning that good earnings (STX, HOOD, NXPI) are getting punished anyway. Sean posted no ticker call — only his 3-day swing-trading challenge kickoff and a motivational post. Your process sides with the watchers: the closest thing to a qualifier shape is MRVL's inside week on a three-week weekly-21EMA hold, with AMD's Buy-Zone bounce behind it; everything else is a breakout day to not chase (TSLA, DELL, ALAB, FSLY), a bounce to watch hold (SNDK, MU, RKLB, CIFR), a failed test (WDC, STX), or a ranked name with no level (NOW, PLTR, KO).

Sources & Methodology
  • Accounts scanned (7): Sean trades @SRxTrades · iain @ohiain · Enrich Trades @enrichtrades · Remz @Remzztrades · Prof @TheProfInvestor · Venu @Venu_7_ · Peter DiCarlo @pdicarlotrader. All seven profiles were readable this window (top ~5 posts visible per account before the login wall). Sean is the exception on content, not readability: he posted no new ticker call in this window, so he has no row.
  • Posts window: Tue Oct 27 – Wed Oct 28, 2026 — everything visible after the Oct 27 feed's window (which ended Oct 27, 06:24 UTC). Logged-out X shows only the ~5 most recent posts per account; posts truncated in the extraction itself (Enrich's “It's All Over” portfolio after its first name, Enrich's 10/28 watchlist tail, Prof's ALAB stop and SPY statistic, iain's timing post, Sean's challenge post) are quoted only to the visible cutoff. Where a post is truncated, the feed says so instead of guessing the rest.
  • Price data: Yahoo Finance daily data, as of the Tue Oct 27, 2026 close — this run is pre-market Wednesday, so Tuesday's close is the latest completed close and Wednesday's session is not in any number here. Moves described as “overnight” (Prof's SKHY +6.8% and MU rocket) happened after that close and are reported as the trader's figures, with no price invented for them. Trader-stated = a level or call from their post, attributed by name. Chart check = computed by us from that data — it can confirm or push back on a trader's framing, and it's labeled every time. The 200-day SMA figures for SNDK, WDC and STX and the weekly 21EMA figure for MRVL are our checks, since the dataset's standard levels are the 50-day EMA, 30-week MA and 50-week EMA.
  • Sector lines: each card's sector/industry ETF comparison (Yahoo Finance, Tue Oct 27, 2026 close) — close, day change, Weinstein stage by the same 30-week MA method, and price vs the 50-week EMA. Mappings: AAPL/DELL→XLK, MSFT/NOW/PLTR→IGV, NVDA/SNDK/MRVL/ALAB/MU/AMD/AVGO/WDC/STX/NXPI→SMH, GOOGL/META→XLC, AMZN/TSLA→XLY, FSLY→CLOU (cloud computing — best fit), RKLB→UFO (space — best fit), SKHY→EWY (South Korea — best fit for the KOSPI name), KO→XLP (consumer staples — best fit), HOOD→FINX (fintech — best fit), CIFR→WGMI (bitcoin miners — best fit), BTC→IBIT (spot bitcoin). Best-fit choices are noted here, not hidden.
  • Where none of the seven commented, the section says Unavailable / no trader signal — never “unchanged.” All four indexes are unavailable this window: no trader posted an index-specific level or trade call (the SPY panel carries Prof's midterm statistic and iain's caution note as context, and the QQQ panel carries Remz's flat-tape note, but none names an index level, so the strip labels stay unavailable, as in yesterday's feed).
  • Qualifier rules (constructive pullback into a key MA/support, tightening base near highs, confirmed breakout; never extended/chased). Closest qualifier shapes, none fired clean: MRVL (inside week on a three-week weekly-21EMA hold) and AMD (bounce inside DiCarlo's Buy Zone) — both pending confirmation, so both carry amber chips. Constructive holds, not entries: PLTR, AAPL (holds-only at the highs). Bounce/test watches, not qualifiers: SNDK (200-day test into earnings), MU (overnight rocket, unconfirmed by a close), RKLB ($59 gap-fill watch in a Stage 4 name), SKHY (overnight move, no trend read), CIFR (base forming in a Stage 4 name), AVGO (thesis, no trigger), FSLY (base building into Nov 4 earnings). Failed tests: WDC, STX (both below the 200-day). Ranked with no level: NOW, PLTR, KO (Leadr top 5 via Enrich). Strong days to not chase: TSLA, DELL, ALAB, FSLY. Explicitly not qualifiers: MSFT/NVDA/GOOGL/AMZN/META (chart checks only), HOOD/NXPI (earnings-punished names below trend).
  • Coverage note: nothing is carried over silently. Yesterday's ideas appear here only where today's posts repeat them (RKLB, TSLA, MRVL, MU, SNDK, PLTR, NOW, AVGO, SKHY) — and then only under today's calls, which sometimes differ from yesterday's (MRVL/MU were Sean's shorts on Oct 25 and Prof's bounce/overnight names today; RKLB's $55 reclaim from yesterday is now cleared on our check). INTC, QCOM, BE, LMT, XOM, LITE, IREN, CRWV, NFLX, APP and the rest of yesterday's board are not rows because today's posts do not repeat those calls.
  • Badge key: Setup describes structure only (green = constructive, amber = pending confirmation, red = broken/extended). Coverage counts the traders behind a name and is always gray — “Chart only” means no trader mentioned it and implies nothing about the setup. Stage lives in the pill next to each ticker (30-week MA basis) and is kept out of the prose and the setup badges; traders' own quoted words are exempt. SKHY carries a “No 30-wk history” pill instead of a stage: too few weekly closes exist for a 30-week MA or 50-week EMA yet.
  • Level strength: Strong = 2+ confluent anchors (52w high/low, 3m swing, 50-day EMA, 30-week MA, 50-week EMA, trader-stated) within 0.75%, or a 52w extreme with 3+ weekly touches in the past year. Moderate = 1 anchor or 2–3 touches. Light = anything else. Touches count weeks whose high or low came within 0.75% of the level. Duplicate prices merge into one row carrying both labels.
  • Trader charts: none embedded this edition. Media URLs exist in the logged-out profile HTML, but they could not be reliably matched to specific posts (the same reason no trader chart was embedded on Oct 26–27), so no trader chart is embedded rather than risking a wrong one.
  • Chart verification gate: every plotted line's endpoint was checked against levels.json before the HTML was built — all computable lines passed within 0.5%. The 30-week MA is a true trailing mean over full 30-week windows only. SKHY's 30-week MA and 50-week EMA are not applicable (insufficient history) and are shown as such, not estimated. One gate failure was caught and fixed during this run: the chart script initially cut off a day early (Oct 26 instead of Oct 27), which moved four 50-day EMAs outside tolerance; the cutoff was corrected and the gate re-run clean before any chart shipped.
